comments.author: @mitzisarahitorres
comments.text:
As a wedding planner I can say that the wedding industry is NOT A SCAM. We are hardworking people, that deal with a lot, and run small businesses, employ people in our community, and pay taxes. What the wedding industry HAS become is a luxury industry. There is a difference. Much like flying first class, going to a five-star restaurant, and shopping at Gucci is a luxury, the wedding industry has now become a luxury. The largest problem is that most couples in today's society, are being brainwashed by Instagram and TikTok into believing that it's actually obtainable and accessible. When in fact, it is not. 

Every year the number of couples increases that think that they can get a Instagram worthy wedding for $30,000. Yes, $30,000 is a lot of money! But it's not enough for their aspirations. 

Every year we get more and more couples that are not focused on the actual marriage, but on the spectacle of the wedding. They are doing it for Instagram. For their TikTok followers. To impress their friends. 

There is absolutely nothing wrong with having a smaller event, or going to the courthouse, or having something in your backyard. There is absolutely nothing wrong with having an average wedding, with your closest friends and family. A lot of the couples that are canceling their weddings are not canceling them because the wedding industry is a scam. They are canceling them because they thought they could have a LUXURY EVENT on a non-luxury budget, and when those fees come due they choose to cancel. 

That is the smartest decision for them! If you cannot afford it, then back out while you can. 

You would not BELIEVE The amount of couples that I get that failed to read the fine print, that failed to budget appropriately, that booked a venue that was 50% of their total wedding budget and then our complaining that they can't afford everything else. We get a lot of couples that want to hire us at the last minute to fix all of the mistakes that they made. All of the contracts that they failed to understand. It really really baffles me how grown adults fail to do basic math. Everything adds up. 

As a wedding industry worker we do not work for free. Too many couples are thinking that because they make their own arrangements, that the wedding planner is going to set them up for free. There is a fee for that! That is labor. That is the job of a staff member. When we send them the invoice, they act like we are nickeling and diving them. 

Sorry, I get triggered about all these conversations about the industry being a scam. Are there wedding vendors that Jack up the price as much as possible just to see how much people will pay? Yes! Are most wedding vendors like this. No. We are having to factor in insurance, Taxes, online platforms, social media management, websites, rent, and the rising cost of GOOD labor. McDonald's can afford to hire somebody straight off the street to serve you mediocre food. We cannot! We need to always have the most experienced, trained and groomed people to work your wedding! We are promising you a beautiful day, and that can only happen with professional work. 

Social media has led people to believe that what they see online is average. That what they see online is what everybody has. That what is on social media is their reality as well. The fact is that it is not! 

The other major issue we have right now is that couples are not willing to cut down their guest count to cut down on costs. Again, because of this performative culture and doing everything for Instagram, they want to invite everyone they know. Unfortunately you cannot invite 200 people and expect to have a wedding on a budget. It's just not going to happen! When we present the idea to our clients to cut down their list to 100 guests, they act like I just slapped them. They act the same way when I recommend switching over to a smaller venue, or a more affordable spot. Are you kidding me? It's absolutely insulting to them. 

With that said, I do not support the shaming of couples who spend a lot of money on a wedding. More blessings to them who have it $$$. It comes off as being haters because all people could afford was go to the courthouse and go have lunch in the backyard. Maybe that is enough for you, but for a lot of people it is not. And if they can afford it, why not? 

If you can afford to fly first class comfortably, why wouldn't you? Why would you purposefully go in coach in the middle seat when you have plenty of money in the bank? Same concept.

I could go on and on!

Read your contracts. Do tons of research and understand how much money you actually have for your event. It's all about the actual marriage, not about the wedding. If you have the money spend it! But if you are going to be starting your married life in financial distress, it is not worth it!

To end my super long rant. Yes, a lot of people are choosing to modify or cancel their wedding plans. But a lot more people are wanting to spend more and more money and get married. We have to turn people away all the time! Our business is booming. So this image of a decaying wedding industry is not accurate either.

comments.text: Our wedding was maybe $5,000, including dress, cake, renting a local park that overlooked a lake (no decor!), table & chair rentals, and catering by a local place.  Friends helped set up.  I shopped deals & clearances in the several months leading up to it.  We made our own table centerpieces, my MIL made the corsages & man flowers (only my bouquet and my husband’s boutinere (sp?  I hate that word!) were real.  It was really low key.  We married at our church for free & used the park for reception.  Everyone we loved was there.  And it was awesome! ❤
